title: Kubernetes Teams Get a Safer Way to See Their Own GPU Metrics
gist: Adobe engineers published an open-source, tenant-aware proxy design (NGINX, kube-rbac-proxy, prom-label-proxy, a MetricAccess CRD and optional per-tenant Prometheus) that lets Kubernetes teams safely see their own GPU utilisation and power metrics, exposing idle accelerator spend such as a GPU left at zero utilisation for 11 days.

insights.claim: Adobe engineers found a GPU that remained at zero utilisation for 11 consecutive days despite being allocated and powered on, illustrating that GPU allocation alone does not show whether accelerators do useful work.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Idle-but-allocated accelerators are a hidden cost line; GPU observability tooling targets real AI infrastructure waste.
insights.quote: a GPU that had remained at zero utilisation for 11 consecutive days despite being allocated and powered on
insights.locator: The immediate use case is GPU visibility

insights.claim: Accelerator capacity can represent a significant infrastructure cost, so teams need utilisation and power-consumption visibility to judge whether expensive GPU capacity is actually used.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Rising GPU spend creates demand for utilisation-level FinOps and observability, not just allocation tracking.
insights.quote: Accelerator capacity can represent a significant infrastructure cost, but allocation alone does not indicate whether those GPUs are doing useful work.
insights.locator: The immediate use case is GPU visibility

insights.claim: With GPU utilisation, framebuffer memory, power consumption and request-rate metrics, teams can detect idle GPUs, GPUs drawing power without application traffic, or workloads receiving traffic while GPU capacity stays underutilised.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete query playbook for right-sizing GPU fleets, which can reduce accelerator demand per workload.
insights.locator: With access to metrics such as GPU

insights.claim: A central Prometheus instance can hold metrics from thousands of namespaces, making unrestricted tenant access both a data-exposure risk and a noisy-neighbour performance problem.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Shared telemetry stores become security and scaling bottlenecks as clusters consolidate many teams.
insights.locator: The problem is straightforward but difficult

insights.claim: Adobe's design routes requests through NGINX and kube-rbac-proxy for authentication and authorisation, then a multi-tenant Prometheus proxy that identifies the tenant, discovers backends and restricts queries to that tenant's namespace.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Shows platform teams can solve multi-tenancy by composing existing CNCF components instead of buying a new metrics platform.
insights.locator: The architecture uses existing Kubernetes and CNCF

insights.claim: prom-label-proxy rewrites incoming PromQL queries to enforce a namespace constraint before they reach Prometheus, because relying on developers to include the right namespace is not a sufficient security boundary.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Enforcement at the proxy layer is what makes self-service observability safe in shared clusters.
insights.quote: simply asking developers to include the correct namespace in their queries would not provide a sufficient security boundary

insights.claim: A Kubernetes custom resource called MetricAccess lets teams declare required metrics by exact name, regular expression or PromQL selector, giving self-service while the platform team keeps control of collection and access.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Declarative, self-service access patterns reduce platform-team toil as tenant counts grow.
insights.locator: The platform also introduces a Kubernetes custom

insights.claim: With metricIsolation enabled and per-tenant remote-write, one example configuration cut a tenant's stored series from more than 10,000 to roughly 300.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: A ~97% series reduction shows curated per-tenant storage can sharply cut observability storage and query costs.
insights.quote: one example configuration reduced a tenant's stored series from more than 10,000 to roughly 300
insights.locator: Adobe reports that one example configuration

insights.claim: Data never collected into a tenant's Prometheus cannot later be exposed through that store, so curated collection acts as a second isolation boundary on top of query filtering.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Minimising collected data is both a cost and a security control, a design principle applicable beyond metrics.
insights.quote: data that is never collected into the tenant's store cannot subsequently be exposed through that store
insights.locator: Adobe reports that one example configuration

insights.claim: Splitting roles lets the central Prometheus keep infrastructure-wide collection while tenant Prometheus instances serve team dashboards and queries, so the shared system no longer has to answer every developer's routine queries.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Offloading read traffic from shared telemetry reduces the need to over-provision central observability infrastructure.
insights.locator: This separation also changes the operational model

themes.theme: Shared Kubernetes platforms for AI workloads

insights.claim: Tenant-aware observability is increasingly relevant as Kubernetes clusters become shared platforms for application, data and AI workloads, where platform teams must give observability without creating a security risk or performance bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Points to growing demand for multi-tenant platform tooling as AI workloads land on shared Kubernetes clusters.
insights.locator: This is increasingly relevant as Kubernetes

insights.claim: The architecture is not GPU-specific; the underlying pattern is a tenant-aware observability layer of authentication, query isolation, curated metric access and optional per-tenant storage.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: The pattern generalises, broadening its relevance beyond GPU fleets to any multi-tenant platform.
insights.locator: Although GPUs provide the most obvious

insights.claim: Grafana Mimir builds multi-tenant isolation into its architecture using tenant identifiers and an authentication layer, and Cortex uses a similar X-Scope-OrgID model, whereas Adobe keeps a shared Prometheus and wraps it with Kubernetes-aware access controls and namespace filtering.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Open-source wrappers around vanilla Prometheus compete with purpose-built multi-tenant stores like Mimir and Cortex-based managed services.
